summary: Compose Telegram HTTPS URL buttons through the tenant-scoped Social API and leased publication worker.

impacts.evidence: Buttons are loaded only through tenant-scoped Social Core variants and connector-account capability settings.
Only bounded user-visible labels and HTTPS URLs are persisted; callback data, secrets and provider payloads are excluded.
SocialPublicationCreate and SocialPublication gain an optional buttons array; generated SDKs are regenerated from OpenAPI.
Existing safe social events carry IDs/state and do not copy content or button values.
The existing provider-neutral SocialPublishRequest mapping is populated from the new Core snapshot; SDK-v1 operation interfaces remain additive.
Migration 000042 adds a default-empty JSONB button snapshot and updates the capability validator with static migration checks.
Core, API and database enforce HTTPS-only URLs, bounded labels/counts and reject callback payloads/extra fields.
The existing publication capability, tenant account setting, worker lease and receipt recovery gates remain mandatory.
Existing content/variant/publication audit and outbox records remain the source lineage; raw button data is not copied to audit summaries.
Telegram ambiguous-write recovery remains non-retryable and receipt-based; no new provider idempotency assumption is introduced.
Only the existing Telegram sendMessage/sendPhoto/sendVideo egress is used; callback and inbound webhook surfaces remain closed.
Existing social worker lease, retry/DLQ, timeout and rate-limit telemetry covers button publications.
Disabling Telegram social.post.buttons or removing the account setting prevents new button publications while existing variants remain readable.
Core, worker, existing Telegram adapter, OpenAPI/SDK, migration and frontend validation cover success and invalid-button paths.
